answer: An agent marketplace locks a separate $100 bond for each identity accepting a job, whether it grades a walnut harvest, translates a sonnet, or diagnoses a vine disease. A contract forfeits the bond if no result arrives by the agreed deadline, and each identity can hold only one job at a time. Creating names is free, but occupying 1,000 job slots requires $100,000 in locked capital; abandoning those jobs burns it.
